best_for: Freelancers, students and anyone curious about their own screen time who want automatic tracking that stays on their own computer.

points.title: Tracks by itself
points.text: It records which app and window title is in front, without timers to start. Browser extensions for Chrome and Firefox add the active tab, and editor plugins add coding time.

points.title: Your data stays local
points.text: Everything is stored on your device and never uploaded to a cloud by default. You can export, back up or delete it whenever you like.

points.title: Free with no gates
points.text: ActivityWatch is open source under the MPL 2.0, with no ads, usage limits or locked features. An optional AW Pro subscription starts at USD 5 per month, and one-off donations are welcome. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Sync is not finished
points.text: The project lists syncing between devices as work in progress, so each computer keeps its own history for now.

points.title: A dashboard in your browser
points.text: The tray app starts a local server and the watchers, and you read your data at `http://localhost:5600`. If you use a proxy, add `127.0.0.1` to `NO_PROXY` first.

points.title: System needs
points.text: It runs on 64-bit Windows 10 or later and macOS 12 or later, with separate Apple silicon and Intel builds since 0.14. The Windows installer can install for the current user or for the whole machine.

points.title: Linux is not listed here
points.text: The project ships Linux builds as .zip, AppImage and .deb, needing glibc 2.35, and handles Wayland from 0.14.2. This site lists only Windows, with 10 versions, and macOS with the current release.
